Answer to the question: "What is the Pearson correlation coefficient between gene length and mean expression (across samples) for protein-coding genes in CD4 immune cells?"

PRIMARY RESULT (approved design, variant a): Pearson r = 0.0617 (r = 0.061697, p = 2.77e-18, n = 19,942 protein-coding genes, mean of raw batch-corrected read counts across the 151 CD4 samples). In short, the Pearson correlation is approximately 0.06 — a very weak positive linear association.

Sensitivity variants:
- (b) Excluding the 1,518 protein-coding genes that are all-zero in CD4: r = 0.0528, p = 7.28e-13, n = 18,424.
- (c) Length vs log1p(mean expression): r = 0.3175, n = 19,942 (p < 1e-300).
- Spearman rho (variant-a gene set): 0.4394 — the monotone association is much stronger than the linear one because mean expression is extremely right-skewed (skew = 41.4; median 56.8 vs max 252,736).

Key diagnostics:
- Mean-expression distribution is heavily right-skewed: quartiles 0.52 / 56.8 / 393.5, 99th percentile 7,073, max 252,736 (EEF1A1). A handful of ultra-highly expressed genes act as leverage points; excluding the top 8 (EEF1A1, MT-CO1, TTN, MT-ND4, AHNAK, RNF213, MT-ND2, MT-CO3) raises variant-a r to 0.0960. Note several top-leverage genes are mitochondrial genes with short lengths, which suppress the positive slope.
- All-zero gene count correction: the 14,896 all-zero figure mentioned earlier was across ALL 59,453 genes; restricted to the 19,942 protein-coding set it is 1,518 genes (used in variant b).
- Donor duplicates: within the CD4 subset there are NO donors with replicate libraries (_1/_2) — 0 duplicated donors — so the primary per-sample analysis is unaffected by donor averaging; no correction was needed.
- Data quality: counts matrix has 0 missing values, 0 negatives, all integers; Length has 0 missing values and no zeros/negatives (range 8–347,964 nt).

Interpretation: on the raw-count scale the linear Pearson correlation between gene length and mean CD4 expression is weakly positive (~0.06); the relationship is much stronger in log space or by rank (~0.32–0.44), reflecting the heavy-tailed expression distribution.

Execution evidence: analysis.py in /workspace (executed, nonempty); outputs above are from the actual run.
